out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: Permit to Operate Posted in Conspicuous Location
violations.observation: The establishment has not posted the permit to operate in a conspicuous location. The 2025 health department permit was posted but the 2026 permit was not.
violations.corrective_action: A valid permit shall be posted in every food establishment in a conspicuous place in the public view. Food establishment permits are issued for a calendar year and expire on December 31 regardless of the month of issue. Post the 2026 health permit as soon as possible or before, the next routine inspection not to exceed six months.

violations.title: Food Manager Certificate & Responsibility
violations.observation: There is no Certified Food Manager present in the establishment.
violations.corrective_action: It shall be unlawful to operate a food establishment unless it is under the immediate control of a certified food manager. It is highly suggested that you have more than one employee with the food manager's license. ORS Interactive, Inc. (see handout provided) issues the required photo identification card with proof of successful completion of a certified food manager's exam. Failure to have a certified food manager on site during ALL hours of operation including food preparation, food service, and cleaning/sanitizing of equipment/utensils will result in closure of the establishment. Provide a certified food manager as soon as possible or within 10 days. Follow up is required for this violation on Friday, August 14.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: Observed the handsink at the three compartment sink area used to store soiled equipment.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. The food employee moved the soiled equipment during the inspection to correct

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at each handwashing sink. There were no paper towels provided in the restroom on the bakery side of the establishment.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. Provide paper towels at all hand sinks at all times. Correct as soon as possible or before the next follow up inspection on Friday, August 14.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw chicken was stored over a ready-to-eat sauce in the walk-in refrigerator. Raw eggs were stored over, uncovered, and ready to eat cabbage mixture in the region in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. Both occurrences were corrected by the food employee during the inspection.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: cooked chicken and sausage on the steam table were not being held hot enough and were 127°, 95°, 90°, and 113°. A whole piece of cooked fish was 128º on the steam table.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. Hot food must be held at 135°F and above at all times. The EHS observed that two pans were being used under the food. Steam tables are designed for single pans so that steam can come in contact with the pan holding the food. If double pans are used, the food won’t stay hot enough. The foods were discarded.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: a container of white rice in one of the refrigerators was not being held cold enough 48°F. Chicken in the walk-in refrigerator was 58° and 52°, shredded cheese in the same unit was 48°
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. All the foods listed were discarded due to temperature abuse.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: Observed several foods that are prepared on site, including a chicken mixture, black beans, cooked rice, and other foods were not date marked with expiration dates.
violations.corrective_action: If foods are prepared on site and held for more than 24 hours, they must be date marked with a seven day expiration date. Date mark all foods prepared on site as soon as possible or within 10 days. Follow up is required for this on Friday, August 14.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: a very large container (~4 gallons) of black beans cooked yesterday was sitting on the counter and was 95°F. Two large containers of chicken mix in the walk refrigerator from yesterday was 58°.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. Discontinue cooling large quantities of foods in large containers. The foods must be placed into shallow containers and cooled from 135° to 41° within six hours or less. Correct as soon as possible or before the follow up inspection on Friday, August 14. The beans and chicken mix were discarded due to temperature abuse.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. Observed several foods stored on the floor in the walk-in refrigerator. Foods are also observed Stuart on the floor in other locations in the establishment.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. Discontinue storing foods on the floor of the walk-in refrigerator and in other locations as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed six months.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of grime and debris: there were one appear to be mouse droppings on the unused slicer underneath the counter
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Clean the unused slicer as soon as possible before the next routine inspection, not to exceed six months.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: Observe the light in the restroom was not working.
violations.corrective_action: Repair the physical facilities. Poor repair and maintenance compromises the functionality of the physical facilities. Repair the light in the restroom as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed six months.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at each handwashing sink. There were no paper towels at the handsink next to the three compartment sink.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. The manager corrected this during the inspection. CDI.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw eggs were stored over salsa and limes in the glass front Coke refrigerator on the bakery side. Raw sausage was stored over cooked chicken in the coke unit on the bakery side.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. The manager moved both items to lower shelving in the refrigerator. CDI.

violations.title: Food Contact Surfaces Clean to Sight & Touch
violations.observation: The following equipment/utensils were observed soiled to sight and touch: the two meat slicers (on unused, one used) were both visibly soiled with food debris and mouse droppings.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to the sight and touch. A surface that is soiled cannot be effectively sanitized. The manager had one of the employees clean the slicers. CDI.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: oatmeal on the steam table was 125º. Red beans on the steam table were 110ºF.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. The manager had a food employee reheat both products to 165º. CDI.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: there were some food items that were not being date marked including a chicken dish in the walk-in and ready to eat foods in the Coke refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. The EHS discussed the date marking requirement for any food prepared on site and held more than 24 hours. CDI.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events. Observed no written vomit and diarrhea procedures on site.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. EHS conducted education regarding importance of written procedures and handed a copy of the written policy to the CFM.

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Water Temp
violations.observation: Observed handwashing sink at front near steam wells at 80F.
violations.corrective_action: A handwashing sink shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 100F through a mixing valve or combination faucet. PIC contacted technician to service hot water.

violations.title: Access to Handwashing Sink
violations.observation: The handwashing facility located near the 3 compartment sink at cook line is blocked by dirty dishes, preventing access by employees for easy handwashing.
violations.corrective_action: A hand washing sink shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for employee use. PIC relocated items.

violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. PIC discarded items.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: Time as a Public Health Control, Written Procedures
violations.observation: The person in charge is not able to provide written procedures for the use of time as a public health control (TPHC) with the following time/temperature control for safety food item(s): fried pork rind at 70F near register (2 hours).
violations.corrective_action: If time only is used as a public health control for a working supply of time/temperature control for safety food before cooking or for ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that is displayed or held for service for immediate consumption, written procedures shall be prepared in advance and maintained in the food establishment and made available to the regulatory authority upon request. EHS explained TPHC procedure and will email written procedures for aforementioned item to PIC.

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: fried pork rind near register.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to- eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. EHS explained TPHC procedure to PIC. PIC provided time mark.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials are not properly stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single service items. Observed glass cleaner and Fabuloso stored in food area near register. Observed Fabuloso cleaner stored directly on canned soy sauce.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored below food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items to prevent contamination. PIC relocated items and understands poisonous and toxic materials shall not be stored near food areas.

violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. violations.title: Food Thermometers, Provided & Accessible
violations.observation: The certified food manager could not provide a food temperature measuring device. PIC was unable to provide food thermometer.
violations.corrective_action: A metal-stemmed probe food thermometer shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures. Please obtain food thermometer by follow up.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Distressed Food Segregated
violations.observation: Products for credit, redemption, or return are not being stored in a separate designated area. Observed gold label soy sauce in yellow can observed with severe dents along seams near cookline.
violations.corrective_action: Store damaged and/or spoiled products in a separate and segregated area to preclude the mistaken use of these products. PIC discarded can.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: observed condiment container in raw, marinated chicken used as scoop, scoop with no handle in rice storage bin, spoons in ambient water.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. PIC removed scoops and spoons from aforementioned food items and understands proper utensils with storage shall be used to handle food items. Please ensure continuous compliance.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: Milk crate(s) found used for the following purpose(s): storage of chicken tamales, wrapped tamales on counter near cook line, shelf-stable cream filling next to 2 DR coca-cola display (3).
violations.corrective_action: Milk crates, soda crates, and/or bread racks are not designed to store or elevate food, equipment, utensils, clean linens, and single-service items. Provide only ANSI-certified (such as NSF-listed) shelving units, storage units, or dunnage racks. PIC obtained stainless steel container to store food items. Please discontinue use of milk crates for storage of any food items and ensure compliance by next routine inspection.

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: 1. 2 DR display near prep line at 44F and 2. 2 DR coke display at 53F. 3. Light bulbs under type 1 hood above fryer, grill, and stoves are burnt out.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. PIC contacted technician to repair refrigerators and technician arrived during inspection. Please replace lightbulbs prior to next routine inspection.

violations.title: Manual Wash Water Temperature
violations.observation: The temperature of the in-use wash water solution was observed at less than 110F. Observed 3 compartment sink at 80F.
violations.corrective_action: The temperature of the wash solution for manual warewashing machine must be no less than 110F or the temperature specified on the cleaning agent manufacturer's label instructions. PIC contacted technician to service hot water.

violations.title: Test Kit/Device for Chemical Sanitizer
violations.observation: There is no test kit located in the facility for monitoring the concentration of the chemical sanitizing solutions. PIC was unable to locate bleach test kit during inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Obtain a BLEACH test kit. Please obtain bleach test kit by the time of follow up.

out_items.name: Hot and cold water available, adequate pressure

violations.title: Hot Water Capacity to Meet Peak Demands
violations.observation: The water heater serving the food service establishment is no longer operable. Observed no hot water throughout the establishment.
violations.corrective_action: Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the food establishment. At this time, a new commercial, approved water heater shall be installed to meet the peak hot water demands. The water heater shall be approved prior to installation. PIC has contacted certified plumber to address issue with hot water heater. EHS will follow up within 10-days. If a replacement is required, please contact EHS to ensure proper replacement is ordered.

violations.title: Air Gaps/Breaks
violations.observation: An air gap between the water supply outlet and the flood rim level for the sanitizing compartment is not observed.
violations.corrective_action: An air gap between the water supply inlet and the flood level rim of the plumbing fixture, equipment, or nonfood equipment shall be at least twice the diameter of the water supply inlet and may not be less than one inch. PIC will contact certified plumber to install proper air gap.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.'
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. Education provided and EH policy put in place.
